- File: scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py | Line or code reference: entry_matches(), line 149: `return fnmatch.fnmatchcase(path, entry)` | Problem: The custom segment-aware globstar matcher `_path_glob_matches` was replaced with `fnmatch.fnmatchcase`. Python's `fnmatch` does NOT implement `FNM_PATHNAME` semantics -- `*` matches `/`. An allowlist entry `scripts/*.sh` now matches `scripts/subdir/run.sh`, which the old path-segment-aware matcher correctly prevented. | Why it fails at runtime: An `ai:scope:scripts/*.sh` label that previously restricted AI edits to top-level scripts now silently permits changes in any subdirectory. This weakens the scope-lock safety boundary in a security-critical enforcement path. Tests at `tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py:207` (`test_cli_explicit_allowlist_file_supports_scope_lock_glob`) and `tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:1592-1593` assert the old `--allowlist-file` path. | SEVERITY: MAJOR | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

Downstream parsing of diagnose results expects these keys. The test suite will fail on the missing keys (lines 1729-1730, 1826-1828, 2268-2269). | SEVERITY: BLOCKER | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py | Line or code reference: `_sync_memory_reference_files`, lines 220-243 | Problem: The dual-directory schema resolution (copy consumer schemas first, then backfill missing schemas from `SUPPORT_AI_MEMORY_DIR`) was replaced with a single-source fallback. If the consumer repo has its own `schemas/` directory, the support directory is completely ignored. Previously, schemas from the support directory would be copied as backfill for any schema files not yet vendored into the consumer repo. Now, if the consumer has even one schema file, the support directory contributes nothing. | Why it fails at runtime: Consumer repos that vendor a partial `ai-memory/schemas/` directory will not receive additive schema files from the workflow-source clone, causing `validate_memory_record` to fail against outdated/incomplete schemas during CI runs. This is a regression from the old backfill behavior. | SEVERITY: MAJOR | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py | Line or code reference: `promote_candidates`, line 1747 (removed `_is_prune_marked` guard), `retrieve_memory_context`, line 2096 (removed `_is_prune_marked` guard), `compact_memory`, line 2324 (removed `prune_marked_at` archiving condition and prune+delete condition) | Problem: The `_is_prune_marked` guard was removed from `promote_candidates` (no longer skips prune-marked records), `retrieve_memory_context` (prune-marked candidates are now retrieved), and `compact_memory` (prune_marked_at no longer triggers archiving; prune+delete no longer considers prune marking). Since `_is_prune_marked`, `mark_candidate_records_for_prune`, and the entire prune/mark subsystem were removed, existing prune-marked records on the ai-memory branch will behave differently: they will be promoted instead of skipped, retrieved instead of filtered, and will not be compacted or deleted by the prune-marking path. | Why it fails at runtime: If any records in the ai-memory branch carry `prune_marked_at` timestamps from prior runs, they would now silently re-enter the active pipeline (promoted/surfaced in retrieval context) instead of staying suppressed. This is a silent behavioral regression for the memory subsystem that conflicts with the intent of previously issued prune operations. | SEVERITY: MAJOR | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
